samples.summary: Covered destination cells cleared by the merge propagation never consume their spill-blocker registration, so a blocked spill anchor stays stuck at #SPILL!
samples.evidence: The new block (sheet.ts:2394-2421) copies the `removeData` cleanup contract for the *anchor* side (clearSpillBlockers + ghost deletion) but omits the *blocker* side. In `removeData` (sheet.ts:1151-1152) every cell that is cleared runs `const blockedAnchor = this.consumeSpillBlocker(sref); if (blockedAnchor) unblockedAnchors.add(blockedAnchor);` and those anchors are then force-added to `changedSrefs`/`dependantsMap` (sheet.ts:1163-1166) so the spill can re-attempt. `setData` does the same at sheet.ts:1082-1086. Here the cell at `ref` is deleted (line 2419) or reduced to style-only (line 2417), i.e. the obstruction is gone, but `this.spillBlockers` still maps that sref to the waiting anchor and the anchor is never added to `changedSrefs`. Result: the spill anchor keeps its stale #SPILL! value forever (until an unrelated edit touches it), and the stale blocker entry remains in `spillBlockers` so a later `setData` on that cell will resurrect a recalculation for an anchor that may no longer exist. The same omission applies to the ghost cells deleted at lines 2408-2409.

read the whole moveRangeTo body for any consumeSpillBlocker call

samples.summary: `if (cell.spillAnchor) continue;` leaves spill ghost content hidden under the newly propagated merge, which is exactly the state the surrounding loop exists to prevent
samples.evidence: The loop's own comment (lines 2385-2388) states covered cells must hold no content, "otherwise they stay hidden under the merge and reappear when it is removed." The new guard at line 2397 skips ghost cells, so a destination cell that is a spill ghost keeps its value under the merge and will reappear on unmerge, breaking the invariant `mergeSelection` establishes. The symmetric case is also unhandled: a spill anchor located OUTSIDE the merged block whose ghost region extends INTO it is never visited by this loop at all, so its ghosts also remain covered. `removeData` can skip ghosts safely because the user's selection normally contains the anchor too; here the covered region is machine-chosen and need not contain the anchor.

samples.summary: Ghost cells deleted outside the merged block are added to changedSrefs but their anchor's spill state (spillRows/spillCols on the surviving anchor cell) is not reset when the anchor is only style-reduced
samples.evidence: At lines 2416-2417, when the cleared spill anchor has styles, it is rewritten as `{ s: cell.s }`, which drops spillRows/spillCols — consistent. But `changedSrefs` gains the deleted ghost srefs (line 2409) while the anchor sref itself is added only via the covered-sref loop (line 2391), which is correct only when the anchor lies inside the merged block. Since ghost deletion is driven from the anchor found inside the block, this holds today; however no invalidation is emitted for formulas that referenced the deleted ghosts' *former aliases* outside the merge if the merge cover map changed concurrently. Low confidence — surfaced for verification.

verdict.reason: The merge-propagation block at sheet.ts:2389-2421 clears covered destination cells (style-only at 2417, delete at 2419) and does the anchor-side spill cleanup (clearSpillBlockers at 2401/2414 + ghost deletion 2402-2412), but never performs the blocker-side half of the contract it cites. consumeSpillBlocker is private (sheet.ts:977-981) and its only two call sites in the whole repo are setData (sheet.ts:1082) and removeData (sheet.ts:1151); no call exists anywhere in moveRangeTo. No indirect rescue path exists either: calculator.ts only registers (117) and clears-by-anchor (130) and never scans spillBlockers for stale entries; buildDependantsMap is derived from formula references so a blocked anchor is not pulled in when its blocker cell is cleared; redirectFormulasForCut (2468-2490) recalculates only cells whose formulas it rewrote; and no other code reads spillBlocked to repair anchors. Consequently, clearing a registered blocker in the covered destination region leaves the waiting anchor at ErrValue.REF with spillBlocked:true (calculator.ts:118-126) and leaves a stale spillBlockers entry — a broken invariant / stale-state correctness bug. Only inaccuracy in the report is cosmetic: the stuck value is #REF!, not #SPILL!.

finding.summary: Merge-layout changes are not fully invalidated: covered srefs of deleted/created merges are omitted from `changedSrefs`, leaving stale dependant values
finding.evidence:
In the new merge pass, the only srefs added to `changedSrefs` are the dest cells that actually had a cell object (`if (!cell) continue;` at line 2386, before `changedSrefs.add(sref)` at 2392). Nothing adds the covered srefs of a merge whose *aliasing* changed. Two concrete stale-value paths:

(a) Deleted destination merge, no moved merge. Setup: A1='10', B1 empty, A3='20', merge A3:B3, and D1='=B3' (displays 20 through the merge alias, since `fetchGridByReferences` resolves local refs via `normalizeRefToAnchor`, sheet.ts:2699). Move A1:B1 → A3. `overwrittenMerges=[A3:B3]` (fully inside destRange) is deleted at 2366-2367, `movedMerges` is empty so the clearing loop never runs. `changedSrefs` = {A3 (movedGrid), A1, B1 (source clear)} — B3 is absent. `expandChangedSrefsWithMergeAliases` therefore never yields B3, `buildDependantsMap` never reaches D1, and D1 keeps the stale 20 although B3 is now an independent empty cell.

(b) Newly created destination merge over an empty source. Setup: merge A1:B1 with no value, A3='20', B3 empty, D1='=B3' (empty). Move A1:B1 → A3. `movedGrid` is empty, so the new merge A3:B3 is created but the covered cell B3 has no stored cell (`if (!cell) continue;`) and is not added to `changedSrefs`; B3 now aliases to A3='20' but D1 is never recalculated.

Compare `unmergeSelection` (sheet.ts:4351-4356) and `mergeSelection` (4299-4302), which deliberately add *every* covered sref of every affected merge to `changedSrefs` precisely because aliasing changed. The move path only adds cells it happened to write or delete.

verdict.reason: The finding claims moveRangeTo omits covered srefs of deleted/created merges from changedSrefs. Both claimed gaps are explicitly handled in the working tree. (a) sheet.ts:2364-2375 iterates `[...movedMerges, ...overwrittenMerges]` and, for each, adds every sref from `mergeCoveredSrefs(merge.anchor, merge.span)` to `changedSrefs` (2370-2371) before `deleteMerge` — the guard at 2364 is an OR, so an overwritten-merge-only move (scenario a, B3) still runs it. (b) sheet.ts:2389-2395: `changedSrefs.add(sref)` at 2391 is the FIRST statement of the covered-sref loop for the newly created destination merge, executed unconditionally BEFORE `if (sref === anchorSref || movedGrid.has(sref)) continue;` (2392) and before `if (!cell) continue;` (2395). The finding's evidence states the opposite ordering (add at 2392 gated by !cell at 2386); the actual code order is reversed, so empty covered cells like B3 in scenario (b) are added. `mergeCoveredSrefs` (856-862) yields the whole rs×cs block, and `rebuildMergeCoverMap()` (2423) runs before `expandChangedSrefsWithMergeAliases` (2431), so expansion sees the post-move layout — the same pattern as mergeSelection (4328-4330) and unmergeSelection (4381-4383).
